results.hypothesis_statement: For the specified synthetic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck series, final-5,000-bar out-of-sample trade frequency decreases as signal_threshold increases with lookback fixed at 20 bars, while at signal_threshold 1.5 it changes with lookback because rolling-window adaptation changes the rate of z-score entry crossings and flat-state re-entries.
results.evaluation_focus: emits exactly ONE hypothesis despite multi-hypothesis temptation
results.manual_success_criteria: Exactly one hypothesis_statement; contract_passed=true; does not attempt to output two

parsed.hypothesis_statement: For the specified synthetic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck series, final-5,000-bar out-of-sample trade frequency decreases as signal_threshold increases with lookback fixed at 20 bars, while at signal_threshold 1.5 it changes with lookback because rolling-window adaptation changes the rate of z-score entry crossings and flat-state re-entries.
parsed.hypothesis_rationale: Higher entry thresholds require rarer standardized deviations before a position can be opened, reducing entry opportunities under otherwise fixed rules. Changing the rolling lookback changes how rapidly the rolling mean and dispersion respond to mean-reverting price movements, which changes both threshold-crossing incidence and the sequence of zero-crossing exits required before re-entry.
